sections.h2: Which county offices serve a Fort Myers property owner?
sections.html:
The Lee County Property Appraiser values Fort Myers property; the Lee County Tax Collector issues bills and accepts money. Those two county offices are the ones you deal with.

Property appraiser questions about value, exemptions and mailing address go to leepa.org or 239-533-6100. The tax collector answers payment questions at 239-533-6000. The tax collector's FAQ points out that levying authorities, listed on your bill, answer questions about ad valorem taxes and non-ad valorem assessments.

sections.h2: When are Fort Myers property taxes due?
sections.html:
Per the collector, payment opens November 1 and full payment is due March 31 of the next year.

Paying in November earns the largest early-payment discount, which the state prints as 4 percent, falling to 3 in December, 2 in January and 1 in February. Anything still owed April 1 is under delinquent-tax law.

sections.h2: How can I pay in Fort Myers?
sections.html:
Lee County's tax collector lists six ways to pay.

  • Online through its pay site, with a printable receipt.
  • Kiosks at any of six service centers, using card or e-check; e-check payments are free.
  • Drop-off at secure SmartLockers open around the clock at the downtown Fort Myers, South Fort Myers, Cape Coral and Lehigh Acres centers, while the Bonita Springs center takes drop-offs inside during business hours. Allow five business days.
  • By phone at 239-533-6000.
  • By mail, following the instructions on the bill.
  • In person at a service center.

The office says it processes payments within two business days of receipt, and the account history on its site shows PAID or UNPAID.

sections.h2: Can I pay in installments or over time in Fort Myers?
sections.html:
Yes, through the installment plan, the partial payment plan or homestead deferral, each with its own rules.

Lee County payment plans, from the Lee County Tax Collector
PlanKey terms
Installment planApply November 1 to April 30; taxes over $100 per notice; four payments due June 30, September 30, December 31 and March 31, with discounts of 6, 4.5 and 3 percent on the first three
Partial payment planOpen to the current year; up to five payments an account; no discount; not taken online, and not for delinquent bills
Homestead deferralApply by March 31; age, income and lien limits; fire insurance naming the tax collector

The collector's page says an installment application for the 2027 tax year can be submitted between November 1, 2026 and April 30, 2027, and that if a property sells mid-plan, the new owner must continue the plan for that year.

sections.h2: What happens if I miss an installment in Lee County?
sections.html:
Missing the first installment by July 31 removes you from the plan, and the tax notice is then mailed by November 1. You must reapply the next year.

  • A missed second or third payment is added to the next installment.
  • Any missed installment forfeits the discount.
  • The first payment is one quarter of the previous year's gross tax, and later payments may include half of any adjustment to current taxes.
  • Once enrolled and paid, you need not reapply yearly, so long as the first installment is made each year.

Anything unpaid on April 1 is handled under delinquent-tax law.

sections.h2: Does Amendment 3 change my Fort Myers bill?
sections.html:
According to the collector, Amendment 3 leaves the 2026 bill alone; that bill is due by March 31, 2027.

Its FAQ states the amendment takes effect January 1, 2027, and that any applicable changes would show up on next year's bills. For how the change affects your exemptions or assessment, ask the Lee County Property Appraiser.

sections.h2: How does the August notice help a Fort Myers owner plan?
sections.html:
The TRIM notice (Form DR-474) arrives in August and shows proposed taxes. Taxing authorities then hold public hearings in September and October on tentative budgets and millage, and in October and November on final budgets and rates.

The tax bill itself is mailed in November. A value challenge is filed with the clerk within 25 days of the notice. Owners who see a surprise in August have time to check exemptions with the Lee County Property Appraiser before the bill arrives.

sections.h2: How do the state limits affect a Fort Myers assessment?
sections.html:
Save Our Homes keeps a homestead's yearly increase to 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower, and the state chart prints 2.9 percent for 2025. Other property can rise 10 percent a year.

The Lee County Property Appraiser's home page offers video guides on the homestead exemption and portability, on the non-homestead assessment limitation and on estimating property taxes. They are worth a few minutes before you sell or buy, since a sale lifts the property to just value and the cap starts over.

sections.h2: What does homestead exemption cover for a Fort Myers owner?
sections.html:
State guidance describes up to $50,000 in two layers. The opening $25,000 reduces every levy including school taxes; the second layer, up to another $25,000, sits above $50,000 of assessed value and spares only non-school levies.

  • The application is Form DR-501, filed with the appraiser, due March 1.
  • You must live there permanently as of January 1.
  • The exemption ends if the unit is rented, stops being your permanent home, or you stop being a Florida resident.
  • Older, disabled and veteran owners may have extra relief; ask the appraiser.

sections.h2: What changes for taxes when a Fort Myers house sells?
sections.html:
The whole year's bill is mailed to the owner of record, with each side's share handled by the closing agent.

The tax collector explains that a change of ownership is recorded with the Clerk of Court and then sent to the appraiser, so a seller may still receive a bill because of timing. Mortgage companies that no longer hold a loan may still appear on the notice, so confirm there is no leftover escrow. The next owner applies for their own homestead by March 1.

sections.h2: What if a Fort Myers tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
Taxes unpaid on April 1 are delinquent, and by June 1 the tax collector sells certificates on them to the bidder who will accept the lowest interest rate, in quarter-percent steps.

  • The certificate holder may not press the owner for two years after that April 1.
  • Then the holder can seek a tax deed, paying a $75 application fee.
  • The clerk runs the auction; the top bidder posts a deposit of 5 percent or $200, whichever is larger.

Selling before any of that happens keeps the payoff at closing simple.

sections.h2: Is there a rental angle for Fort Myers owners?
sections.html:
Yes. The Lee tax collector notes that tangible personal property used on a home's rental activity, such as furniture and appliances, can bring a separate tangible tax bill.

If you recently bought a home that is no longer rented, call the property appraiser's tangible office at 239-533-6140. Separately, renting out a homestead can end the exemption under state rules.

faqs.q: How do I pay Lee County tax on a Fort Myers home?
faqs.a: Pay the Lee County Tax Collector online, by phone at 239-533-6000, by mail, or at a service center. Six service centers have kiosks.
Phone 239-533-6100, the appraiser's number. Exemptions, values and mailing addresses live there.

faqs.q: When does the installment plan application close?
faqs.a: It closes April 30 of the tax year, and applications for 2027 taxes open November 1, 2026. The first payment is due by June 30.

faqs.q: Why did I get a bill after selling?
faqs.a: The roll lists the owner of record when it is sent, and a recent sale may not have reached the appraiser. Pass the bill to the buyer or closing agent.

faqs.q: Can I pay delinquent Fort Myers taxes by check?
faqs.a: No. Delinquent real estate taxes cannot be paid by personal check or eCheck, so ask the collector what forms it takes.
